findings.body: `None.has_global_access` raises AttributeError, producing an unhandled 500 for every audit-log request from non-member callers, including callers that were previously served correctly by the DateTimePaginator path.
findings.failure_mode: Unhandled exception in the request path for callers without org membership.
findings.impact: `None.has_global_access` raises AttributeError, producing an unhandled 500 for every audit-log request from non-member callers, including callers that were previously served correctly by the DateTimePaginator path.
findings.root_cause: New gating expression dereferences the optional `member` field of RpcUserOrganizationContext without a None check.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the member access, e.g. `organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access`, before dereferencing.
findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, causing AttributeError
findings.trigger: A superuser (in a non-elevated session, so `request.user.is_superuser` is evaluated but the short-circuit does not apply for token/staff users) or any authorized caller without an active organization membership (e.g. org:write API token, or superuser not a member of the org) issues GET on the audit log endpoint. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is documented as None when the user_id has no membership.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 71 shows `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is accessed unconditionally. Repository context confirms `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be None (line 346: `member: RpcOrganizationMember | None = None`). When member is None, accessing `.has_global_access` raises AttributeError.

validated_findings.body: `math.ceil`/`math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError, so the optimized branch returns a 500 for every non-empty audit-log page.
validated_findings.impact: `math.ceil`/`math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError, so the optimized branch returns a 500 for every non-empty audit-log page.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new paginator copies the integer-key implementation from `Paginator` while being used with a DateTimeField order_by.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Derive OptimizedCursorPaginator from DateTimePaginator (or reuse its multiplier-based `get_item_key`) so datetime sort keys are converted to numeric cursor values.
validated_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor to a datetime field
validated_findings.trigger: An authorized user calls the audit log endpoint with `?optimized_pagination=true`; the paginator is constructed with `order_by="-datetime"` and at least one AuditLogEntry row is returned, so `build_cursor` invokes `get_item_key` with `item.datetime` (a `datetime` object).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 838-840 show `get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. The paginator is used with `order_by="-datetime"` (line 80), so `self.key` is `datetime`. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a DateTimeField (confirmed in context). `math.floor` on a datetime raises TypeError.

validated_findings.body: The database rejects or mis-evaluates the comparison between the `datetime` column and a bare number, producing a query error (500) or incorrect page boundaries.

validated_findings.impact: The database rejects or mis-evaluates the comparison between the `datetime` column and a bare number, producing a query error (500) or incorrect page boundaries.
validated_findings.root_cause: Cursor decoding copied from the integer-key `Paginator` although the paginator is used with a datetime sort key.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Convert the cursor value back to a timezone-aware datetime as `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` does, or inherit from DateTimePaginator.
validated_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns a raw cursor value for a datetime column
validated_findings.trigger: A second-page request on the audit log endpoint with `?optimized_pagination=true` and a non-empty cursor value; `build_queryset` then appends `WHERE "datetime" <= %s` with the raw numeric cursor value.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 842-843 show `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` directly (a numeric value). When used with datetime column, `build_queryset` at line 857 will compare datetime column against this numeric value, causing type mismatch in SQL WHERE clause.

validated_findings.body: Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, which `Endpoint.paginate` does not translate (it only catches `BadPaginationError`), so the request returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.

            results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled ValueError escapes as a 500 response on attacker-controllable cursor input.
validated_findings.impact: Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.`, which `Endpoint.paginate` does not translate (it only catches `BadPaginationError`), so the request returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400.
validated_findings.root_cause: New code deliberately passes an unvalidated negative offset into QuerySet slicing based on the false assumption that the ORM handles it.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Reject negative cursor offsets with `raise BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")` as every other paginator in this module does, or clamp with `max(0, cursor.offset)`.
validated_findings.title: Negative-offset slicing raises Django ValueError instead of BadPaginationError
validated_findings.trigger: An authorized user requests `?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-5:0`; `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset` is -5, so the QuerySet is sliced with a negative start index.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 877-882 show when `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices queryset with negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets raise ValueError on negative indexing. `Endpoint.paginate` only catches `BadPaginationError` (line 540), so ValueError escapes as 500.

validated_findings.body: The comment documents behavior the code does not provide (Django raises ValueError on negative slicing), which will lead future changes to propagate negative offsets and produce 500s.

validated_findings.failure_mode: Misleading documentation guides incorrect future changes.
validated_findings.impact: The comment documents behavior the code does not provide (Django raises ValueError on negative slicing), which will lead future changes to propagate negative offsets and produce 500s.
validated_findings.root_cause: Explanatory comment added that contradicts Django's slicing semantics and the actual clamping logic on the next line.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the comment with an accurate description: offsets are clamped to 0 only for forward cursors, and negative offsets are still invalid for QuerySet slicing.
validated_findings.title: Comment asserts negative offsets are safely handled by the queryset, which is false
validated_findings.trigger: Any maintainer reading BasePaginator.get_result and relying on the comment when handling `is_prev` cursors with negative offsets, which are still passed unclamped to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The comment at lines 179-181 in BasePaginator.get_result is misleading, but line 182 shows `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` - the code actually clamps to 0 for non-prev cursors. The comment is inaccurate but the actual code path doesn't allow negative slicing in BasePaginator.
